question: How many days do I have to register my new address in Berlin?
Wie lange habe ich Zeit, mich nach dem Einzug anzumelden?
note: Same content as q01, casual German.

question: Frist zur Anmeldung einer Wohnung bei der Meldebehoerde
note: q01/q02/q03 are one question in three registers. This triple is the register experiment.

question: What is the fine if I register too late?
note: 54(3). Obligation lives in 17, penalty in 54.

question: Someone offered to sell me an address to register at. Is that legal?
note: Needs 19(6) for the prohibition AND 54(1)+(3) for the 50000 figure. Two sections.

question: My landlord will not give me the Wohnungsgeberbestaetigung. What should I do?
Can I use my rental contract instead of the landlord confirmation?
note: Only the Berlin pages say this. Not in the BMG at all.

question: How long does my landlord have to give me the move-in confirmation?
note: 19(1) refers to the period in 17(1) rather than stating it. Cross-reference resolution.

question: What must the landlord confirmation contain?
note: 19(3), four-item list.

question: Can I register online with an electronic residence permit?
note: Online registration is NOT possible with an eAT. Buried in a bullet list. Critical for non-EU students.

question: I am a non-EU student. Can I do the Anmeldung from home online?
note: Same fact as q10 phrased as a personal situation. Requires connecting 'non-EU' to the citizenship requirement.

question: Do I need a BundID account to register online?
I live abroad and I am in Berlin for 2 months only. Do I have to register?
note: 27(2) third sentence: three months for people otherwise resident abroad.

question: I am already registered in Germany and subletting in Berlin for 5 months. Do I need to register again?
note: Six months, not three. q13 and q14 sit in the same paragraph with different answers - precision test.

question: How long can I stay in Berlin without registering at all?
note: Trap: 17 looks relevant but has no answer. The answer is in 27 and depends on circumstances.

question: I am living in a hostel while flat-hunting. Do I need to register?
note: 29(1). Note 29 and 27 both use three months but for different situations.

question: Do I have to register if I sleep in a caravan on a campsite?
note: 29(4). Deep in a split section - tests whether later chunks are reachable.

question: Is a caravan a Wohnung under the registration law?
note: 20, last sentence. Interacts with q17 - both about caravans, different sections.

question: What counts as a Wohnung under the registration law?
note: 20. Shortest section in the corpus, always a single chunk.

question: I have a flat in Munich and one in Berlin. Which is my main residence?
note: 21(2) defines it; 22 gives tie-breaks.

question: I am married and my family lives in Hamburg while I study in Berlin. Which flat is my Hauptwohnung?
note: 22(1) overrides the general rule in 21(2). Retrieving 21 alone gives a wrong answer.

question: Was ist der Unterschied zwischen Hauptwohnung und Nebenwohnung?
My main residence changed. How long do I have to tell the authority?
note: 21(4), not 17(1). Same deadline, different obligation - easy for retrieval to confuse.

question: Can I register my second flat online in Berlin?
note: Nebenwohnung registration is in-person only. Contrasts with the Hauptwohnung page.

question: When do I have to deregister from my flat?
note: 17(2) applies only if NOT moving to another residence in Germany. Tests whether the condition survives.

question: How early can I deregister before I move out?
note: 17(2) second sentence.

question: Who registers a child under 16?
note: 17(3), middle of the section.

question: What data is on the Meldebescheinigung?
note: 18(1), five-item numbered list. Direct test of whether lists survived chunking.

question: Is the electronic Meldebescheinigung free?
note: 18(3), at the very end of the section.

question: Does the Anmeldung cost anything?
Are diplomats required to register in Germany?
note: 26 is Befreiung, 27 is Ausnahmen. Adjacent sections, different concepts - confusion test.

question: What documents do I bring to the Buergeramt appointment?
note: 23(1) legally, plus the Berlin page operationally. Both are valid answers.

question: How many days per year can I work on a student residence permit?
note: 16b(3): 140 Arbeitstage (Arbeitstagekonto). NOTE: 280 half-days is a derived figure, not in the text.

question: If I work 3 hours in a day, does that count as a full working day?
note: 16b(3) no. 1: up to four hours counts as half a working day. Deep in a split section.

question: Do student assistant jobs at the university count towards my working days?
note: 16b(3): studentische Nebentätigkeiten are not counted. One sentence, easy to miss.

question: How long is a student residence permit valid?
note: 16b(2): as a rule two years, minimum one year.

question: I am on a language course visa. How many hours per week can I work?
note: 16f(3): 20 hours per week for language course permits. Different rule from 16b - trap if 16b is retrieved.

question: Can I stay in Germany to look for a job after I graduate?
note: 20(1) no. 1 and 20(2): up to 18 months, subsistence must be secured.

question: My residence permit expires next month but my appointment is in three months. What happens?
note: 81(4) and 81(5). One of the most-asked real questions in Berlin.

question: What are the general conditions for getting a residence permit?
note: 5(1). This is where the blocked-account requirement originates.

question: How much money do I need in my blocked account?
note: The amount is set by ordinance, not in AufenthG. 5(1) requires secured subsistence but gives no figure. The system must not invent one.

question: How much does public health insurance cost for students?
note: Not in the corpus at all.

question: Can I bring my spouse to Germany on a student visa?
note: Family reunification is AufenthG 27-36, deliberately excluded from the corpus.

question: Which Buergeramt has the shortest waiting time?
note: Not answerable from documents. The branch list was stripped as navigation.
